source_title: Nigeria Labour Force Survey Q4 2022 & Q1 2023 Report
methodology_changes: Working age population changed from 15-64 to 15 years and above
Employment threshold reduced from 20 hours to 1 hour per week
Underemployment threshold changed from 20-39 hours to less than 40 hours
Questionnaire updated from 13th ICLS to 19th ICLS model
Data collection changed from cross-sectional to continuous throughout the year
Sample increased from 33,300 to 35,520 households annually
Interview period extended from 17-21 days to 40 days per quarter
comparison_with_regional_data: Nigeria's unemployment rate of 4.1-5.3% is in line with the ILO modelled average for Western and Central Africa region (4.7% for 2022). The pattern of low unemployment but high poverty rates is similar to Nigeria's neighbours: Benin (1.8% unemployment, 19.9% poverty), Cameroon (4.1%, 25.7%), Ghana (3.9%, 25.2%), Chad (1.5%, 30.9%), Niger (0.7%, 50.6%).
key_findings: About three-quarters of working-age Nigerians were employed (73.6% Q4 2022, 76.7% Q1 2023)
One-third of employed persons worked less than 40 hours per week
Over 92% of employed Nigerians are in informal employment
Wage employment is only 11.8-13.4% - most Nigerians are self-employed
Post-secondary educated have highest unemployment (9.0% Q4 2022) - seeking formal wage jobs
Women face higher unemployment and underemployment than men
Working poor phenomenon is common - employment does not guarantee escaping poverty
Previous Q4 2020 methodology reported 33.3% unemployment - not comparable due to methodology changes
